summary: This Dockerfile sets up a PHP 8.3 web server with Apache, installing SSL certificates and a custom site configuration, then enabling the necessary Apache modules and disabling default sites in favor of a custom HTTPS-enabled site.

explanations.3: This pulls the official PHP 8.3 image that comes with Apache pre-installed as the base for our container.
explanations.5: This copies an SSL certificate file from the host machine into the container so Apache can use it for HTTPS connections.
explanations.6: This copies the private key for SSL into the container — Apache needs this along with the certificate to encrypt HTTPS traffic.
explanations.8: This copies a custom Apache configuration file into the sites-available directory, which is where Apache looks for site configurations.
explanations.10: The `a2enmod` commands enable Apache modules — `ssl` is needed for HTTPS support, and `rewrite` allows URL rewriting rules.
explanations.12: This disables Apache's default HTTP and HTTPS sites so they won't interfere with our custom configuration.
explanations.13: This enables our custom site configuration file that we copied in earlier.
